To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the detection of FAH in humans is a useful tool to identify high-risk patients and that FAH in animals are an important tool for the evaluation of the carcinogenic potential of chemical agents.

FAH are the most frequent type of preneoplasms observed in animals and humans; that FAH are phenotypically similar in animals and humans, and that FAH are a useful target for risk identification and early detection of neoplasia.

the phenotypic changes of the cellular constituents of FAH are the result of a multistage process of neoplastic progression, which is similar in different experimental and human models, and which can be used for risk identification in animals and early detection in humans.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification and characterization of hepatic pre neoplasia in experimental animals and humans, and the evaluation of their potential for risk identification and early detection of human hepatocarcininogenesis.

the elucidation of the molecular biological mechanisms underlying the development of FAH and their role in carcinogenesis, the identification of FAH in humans, and the evaluation of their diagnostic and predictive value in risk identification and early detection of neoplasia.
the development of a risk identification system based on the detection and evaluation of FAH in the liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
preneoplastic hepatocellular FAH are the best available morphological markers for early detection and identification of hepatocarcinogenic risks in both animals and humans.

the detection of FAH in humans and in experimental animals is a useful tool for the identification of high-risk individuals and for early diagnosis, and may thus help to prevent the occurrence of liver tumors.
the identification and evaluation of preneoplasias, such as FAH, is of paramount importance in both animal and human carcinogenesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the identification of FAH is of paramount importance for risk identification and early detection of neoplasia, and that the morphometric evaluation of FAH is indispensable for a correct interpretation of the results of bioassays and for a correct evaluation of the risk of developing neoplasia.
FAH can be regarded as the most reliable, specific, and sensitive indicator of hepatocarcinogen exposure and of hepatocellular carcinogenesis.
FAH represent a useful tool to identify and characterize risk factors, and to detect preneoplastic lesions in humans, as well as in animals, at risk for developing hepatocellular neoplasm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FAH can be detected in human liver biopsies, and that their presence in patients with chronic liver disease indicates an increased risk for hepatocarcinoma.

FAH represent the earliest stage of hepatocarcinogenic process, and that the identification of FAH in humans may help to identify individuals who are at high risk of developing hepatocellular carcinoma, and thus to implement preventive measures.
the identification of hepatic pre neoplasia in humans and in animal models is of great significance to risk identification and early detection of neoplasia.
